name: Compose Three Classical Ci Poems on Different Seasons
prompt:
Compose three original classical Chinese ci (词) poems — one for each of three different seasons: spring (春), summer (夏), and winter (冬). Save the results to ci_collection.json.

Requirements for each ci poem:
- Use the ci pattern 临江仙 (Lin Jiang Xian): this pattern has two stanzas. The first stanza has 6 lines with character counts 6-6-5-3-6-5. The second stanza also has 6 lines with character counts 6-6-5-3-6-5. (Total 12 lines per poem.)
- The poem must reflect the season in its imagery
- Do NOT copy any existing famous ci poem

Save to ci_collection.json with this exact structure:
{
  "pattern": "临江仙",
  "poems": [
    {
      "season": "春",
      "title": "<title in Chinese>",
      "stanza1": ["<line1>", "<line2>", "<line3>", "<line4>", "<line5>", "<line6>"],
      "stanza2": ["<line1>", "<line2>", "<line3>", "<line4>", "<line5>", "<line6>"],
      "annotation": "<English summary of imagery and mood, 15-50 words>"
    },
    { "season": "夏", ... },
    { "season": "冬", ... }
  ]
}

Each poem must have exactly 3 seasons in the array in this order: 春, 夏, 冬.

criteria.description: ci_collection.json exists in the working directory.
ci_collection.json is valid JSON with a pattern field (string) and a poems field (array).
The pattern field equals the exact string 临江仙.
The poems array contains exactly 3 entries.
The three poems have season values 春, 夏, 冬 in that exact order (index 0, 1, 2).
criteria.testPattern: seasons are 春.*夏.*冬|春, 夏, 冬 in order

criteria.description: Each poem object contains title, stanza1, stanza2, and annotation fields.
Both stanza1 and stanza2 of every poem are arrays of exactly 6 lines.
Every stanza line across all poems is a non-empty string containing at least one Chinese character.
criteria.testPattern: non-empty strings with at least 1 Chinese

criteria.description: Every poem's annotation is a non-empty English string longer than 10 characters.

eval.rubric:
Context: The agent composed three ci poems in the 临江仙 pattern covering three seasons.

Criterion 1: Seasonal Imagery Distinctiveness (Weight: 50%)
1.0: Each poem uses distinctly different and seasonally appropriate imagery — spring has blossoms/warmth, summer has heat/lotus/cicadas, winter has snow/cold/bare trees. The three poems feel noticeably different from each other.
0.5: Two poems have appropriate imagery but one is generic or seasonal imagery overlaps significantly.
0: Poems share the same imagery or seasonal references are absent.

Criterion 2: Poetic Coherence (Weight: 50%)
1.0: Each poem reads as a cohesive whole with consistent emotional tone, and the two stanzas connect thematically. Language is classical and elegant.
0.5: Poems are mostly coherent but some lines feel disconnected or language is too modern.
0: Poems are fragmented or incoherent.
